accepted.name: questions_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  title,
  body,
  accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  comment_count AS comment_count,
  community_owned_date AS community_owned_date,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(favorite_count AS INT64) AS favorite_count,
  last_activity_date AS last_activity_date,
  last_edit_date AS last_edit_date,
  last_editor_display_name AS last_editor_display_name,
  last_editor_user_id AS last_editor_user_id,
  owner_display_name AS owner_display_name,
  owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  post_type_id AS post_type_id,
  score AS score,
  tags AS tags,
  SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) AS view_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
accepted.description: Normalized projection of posts_questions with cleaned numeric casts and preserved identifiers. Use this as the canonical questions relation for downstream joins, aggregations, or time-series. Converts nullable numeric-like STRING fields to INT64 when possible and exposes key metadata. | Use for: time-series of question creation or activity; top questions by score/view_count/answer_count; analysis of accepted answers by question attributes; joins to answers, comments, votes, users

accepted.name: answers_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  title,
  body,
  accepted_answer_id,
  SAFE_CAST(answer_count AS INT64) AS answer_count,
  comment_count AS comment_count,
  community_owned_date AS community_owned_date,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  SAFE_CAST(favorite_count AS INT64) AS favorite_count,
  last_activity_date AS last_activity_date,
  last_edit_date AS last_edit_date,
  last_editor_display_name AS last_editor_display_name,
  last_editor_user_id AS last_editor_user_id,
  owner_display_name AS owner_display_name,
  owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  parent_id AS parent_id,
  post_type_id AS post_type_id,
  score AS score,
  tags AS tags,
  SAFE_CAST(view_count AS INT64) AS view_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
accepted.description: Normalized projection of posts_answers with cleaned numeric casts and preserved identifiers. Use this as the canonical answers relation for downstream joins, aggregations, or to link back to questions via parent_id. | Use for: linking answers to their parent questions; top answers by score/comment_count/view_count; analysis of answerer activity over time or by reputation

accepted.name: users_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  display_name,
  about_me,
  SAFE_CAST(age AS INT64) AS age,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  last_access_date AS last_access_date,
  location,
  reputation AS reputation,
  up_votes AS up_votes,
  down_votes AS down_votes,
  views AS views,
  profile_image_url,
  website_url
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
accepted.description: Cleaned users projection preserving identity and profile metrics. Use for joining post or comment authors to profile attributes like reputation and location. | Use for: join users to posts/comments; user retention and activity analyses; demographic or reputation-based segmentation

accepted.name: comments_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS comment_id,
  text AS text,
  creation_date AS creation_date,
  post_id AS post_id,
  user_id AS user_id,
  user_display_name AS user_display_name,
  score AS score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments`
accepted.description: One row per comment with preserved linkage to post and commenter. Useful for counting comments per post or analyzing comment timelines. | Use for: comment counts per post or per user; comment activity over time; join comments to posts and users

accepted.name: post_votes_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  post_id,
  vote_type_id,
  COUNT(1) AS votes_by_type
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes`
GROUP BY
  post_id,
  vote_type_id
accepted.description: Aggregated vote counts by post_id and vote_type_id. Useful to compute breakdowns of vote types per post (upvotes, accepted, etc.) or to join to posts for total vote measures. | Use for: vote-type distribution per post; total votes by summing votes_by_type; correlate votes with score/comment_count/view_count

accepted.name: question_answer_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  parent_id AS question_id,
  COUNT(1) AS answers_total,
  AVG(score) AS avg_answer_score,
  MAX(score) AS max_answer_score,
  MIN(creation_date) AS first_answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  parent_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  parent_id
accepted.description: Per-question aggregated answer statistics (count of answers, avg answer score, max answer score, first answer time). Use to analyze question response quality and speed. | Use for: questions with fastest first answer; relation between question attributes and answer quality; filtering questions by number or quality of answers

accepted.name: question_tag_exploded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  TRIM(tag) AS tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(COALESCE(q.tags, ''), r'<([^>]+)>')) AS tag
accepted.description: Explodes the tags string on questions into one row per (question_id, tag). Useful for per-tag aggregations or tag-level trend analysis. Assumes tags are whitespace/delimited with angle brackets as in typical StackOverflow exports (e.g. '<sql><bigquery>'). | Use for: tag popularity over time; top tags by question count or aggregate score; join tag-level metrics back to questions or answers

accepted.name: questions_with_user
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.title,
  q.body,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  q.score AS question_score,
  q.view_count AS question_view_count,
  q.answer_count AS question_answer_count,
  u.id AS user_id,
  u.display_name AS user_display_name,
  u.reputation AS user_reputation,
  u.location AS user_location
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
ON
  q.owner_user_id = u.id
accepted.description: Denormalized relation joining normalized questions to user profile data. One row per question with author attributes preserved. Use to analyze question characteristics by author reputation or location. | Use for: impact of asker reputation on answer rate; regional analysis of question topics or outcomes; correlate question metrics with user metrics

accepted.name: answers_ranked_by_score_per_question
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.parent_id AS question_id,
  a.score AS answer_score,
  a.creation_date AS answer_creation_date,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.parent_id ORDER BY a.score DESC, a.creation_date ASC, a.id ASC) AS answer_rank,
  CASE WHEN ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.parent_id ORDER BY a.score DESC, a.creation_date ASC, a.id ASC) = 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_top_answer
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per answer_id with rank within question_id
accepted.description: Ranks answers within each parent question by score descending and provides rank and is_top_answer flag. Useful to select top-N answers per question deterministically downstream by filtering on answer_rank. | Use for: select top-N answers per question; compare top answer characteristics to others; compute metrics for accepted vs top-scoring answers
